text: Riboswitches regulate gene expression via ligand-induced conformational changes between an aptamer domain and an expression platform. Which ligand-to-outcome pairing below is correct?
choices: SAM (S-adenosylmethionine) binding to the SAM-I riboswitch switches translation OFF by sequestering the Shine-Dalgarno sequence in a hairpin
Adenine binding to the add A-riboswitch switches translation OFF by sequestering the start codon
TPP binding to the thi box riboswitch switches translation ON, making it the most widespread riboswitch mechanism in bacteria
Cyclic di-GMP binding to the GEMM riboswitch has no effect on gene expression, serving only as a passive structural sensor
explanation: The SAM-I riboswitch is a translation-OFF switch: SAM binding stabilizes a hairpin that sequesters the Shine-Dalgarno sequence, blocking ribosome access. Choice 1 has the add adenine riboswitch backwards -- ligand binding actually stabilizes the open structure and switches translation ON, not off. Choice 2 similarly reverses the TPP/thi-box riboswitch, which is translation-OFF (though it is correctly described as the most widespread riboswitch class). Choice 3 is wrong because the GEMM (cyclic di-GMP) riboswitch actively controls translation or transcription of its downstream gene rather than acting as a passive, non-regulatory sensor.
